relationship.statement: A pendulum's swing period increases with string length and decreases with stronger gravity, while bob mass has no effect. Release angle sets swing width and max speed, and only slightly lengthens period at large angles.
assumptions: The string is massless and inextensible, with all bob mass at a single point.
Air drag and pivot friction are zero, so total mechanical energy stays constant.
The period formula uses the small-angle approximation (release angles under 15 deg).

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the fixed pivot point to the center of the pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the bob; scales gravitational force and inertia equally so period is unchanged.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle measured from straight down where the bob is released from rest.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration acting on the pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Air drag
quantities.meaning: Friction and air resistance opposing motion, fixed at zero in this ideal model.

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time required for one complete back-and-forth swing cycle.

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of complete swing cycles completed per second (1/T).

quantities.label: Swing angle
quantities.meaning: Instantaneous angle of the string from the vertical equilibrium line.

quantities.label: Max speed
quantities.meaning: Peak speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest point.

quantities.label: Total energy
quantities.meaning: Conserved mechanical energy of the swing, proportional to bob mass.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = inputs.L; var m = inputs.m; var g = inputs.g; var theta0Deg = 12; var theta0Rad = theta0Deg * Math.PI / 180; var T = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / g); var f = 1 / T; var omega = 2 * Math.PI / T; var phase = omega * t; var thetaRad = theta0Rad * Math.cos(phase); var theta = theta0Deg * Math.cos(phase); var oneMinusCos0 = 1 - Math.cos(theta0Rad); var v_max = Math.sqrt(2 * g * L * oneMinusCos0); var E_total = m * g * L * oneMinusCos0; var sinT = Math.sin(thetaRad); var cosT = Math.cos(thetaRad); var bob_x = L * sinT; var bob_y = -L * cosT; var thetaDot = -theta0Rad * omega * Math.sin(phase); var vx = L * thetaDot * cosT; var vy = L * thetaDot * sinT; var vel_tip_x = bob_x + 0.45 * vx; var vel_tip_y = bob_y + 0.45 * vy; var weight_tip_y = bob_y - 0.012 * m * g; var bob_size = 0.25 + 0.75 * (m - 0.5) / 4.5; return { T: T, f: f, theta: theta, v_max: v_max, E_total: E_total, bob_x: bob_x, bob_y: bob_y, vel_tip_x: vel_tip_x, vel_tip_y: vel_tip_y, weight_tip_y: weight_tip_y, bob_size: bob_size, is_heavy_bob: m >= 3.0, is_low_gravity: g < 5.0, is_long_string: L >= 1.8, is_short_string: L <= 0.8 }; }

always: Period depends on L and g, not mass.
Release angle is fixed at 12 deg.

cases.text: Heavy bob raises energy, not T.
Weak gravity slows down the swing.
Long string gives a slow wide arc.

explanation.otherwise: Near Earth gravity with mid length.

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum swing?
lesson.description: Adjust string length, bob mass, and gravity to watch how a pendulum swings from a fixed 12 deg release. Compare the live motion, forces, and angle plot to see what sets the period.
lesson.instructions: Use the sliders to vary string length, bob mass, and gravity. Watch the bob arc, velocity and gravity arrows, live readouts, and the angle-time graph as the pendulum swings.
lesson.goal: Pendulum period increases with string length and decreases with stronger gravity, while bob mass changes total energy and weight without altering the swing period or max speed.
